be sold.
 
10.       Point raised- Rule 8(6) proviso (c)
 Provided that if the sale of such secured assets is being effected by either inviting tenders from the public or by holding public
auction, the secured creditor shall cause a public note in two leading newspapers one in vernacular language having sufficient circulation
in the locality by setting out the terms of sale, which shall include,
     (c) reserve price, below which the property may not be sold.
The word “may” should be replaced by the word “shall” to make the provisions certain that the property shall not be sold below
reserve price.
 
Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
In terms of second proviso to sub-rule (2) of Rule 9, if the Authorised office fails to obtain a price higher than the reserve price, he
may, with the consent of the borrower and the secured creditor effect the sale at such price.  Otherwise, by virtue of first proviso to sub-
Rule (2) of Rule 9, no sale of immovable property shall be confirmed, if the amount offered by sale price is less than the reserve price.  
The exception to sale below the reserve price with the consent of the secured creditor as well as borrower is to meet the situation when
the property is not likely to fetch the price reserved in view of the market condition.  The purpose behind having the word “may” is that it
would enable the secured creditor to sell the property and realize the dues.  It would not be possible if the word “shall” were used.  Using
the word “shall” will mean that property shall not be sold below the reserve price.   As regards any protection for such sales, it is held that
protection to secured creditor is the consent given by the borrower.  Hence, the use of the word ‘may’ in the Rule is apt.
 
11.       Point raised- Rule 8(8)
 
Sale by any methods other than public auction or public tender shall be on such terms as may be settled between the
parties in writing.
Should the settlement between the parties before being finalized be conveyed to the borrower; Secondly should the terms settled
between the parties not be required to be kept open for the sake of transparency?
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
            As at 4 above.  To add, the Rules 6 and 9 provide for sufficient transparency of the transactions of sale.  The authorized officer is
expected to secure the maximum sale price and shall serve to the borrower a notice of thirty days for sale of secured assets including
public notice in Newspapers in case of public auction or invitation of tenders from public.   Further, borrower or secured creditor is not
prohibited from participation in the sale process, i.e. he can bid and purchase the secured assets.
 
12.       Point raised- Rule 9(1)
 Time of sale, Issue of sale certificate and delivery of possession, etc. – (1) No sale, of immovable property under
these Rules shall take place before the expiry of 30 days from the date on which the public notice of sale is published in
newspapers as referred to in the proviso to sub-rule (6) or notice of sale has been served to the Governor.
Different newspaper may publish the public notice on different dates.  How the period of 30 days is computed in such cases?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
The sale of immovable property can take place only after the process of serving/publication of notice is completed.   Hence, the
period of 30 days will be reckoned only from the notice last served or published, as the case may be.
 
13.       Point raised- Rule 9(4)
The balance amount of purchase price payable shall be paid by the purchaser to the authorized officer on or before
the fifteenth day of confirmation of sale of the immovable property or such extended period as may be agreed upon in
writing between the parties.
It is not possible to prescribe a fixed time limit instead of providing for such extended period as may be agreed upon in writing
between the parties so as to complete the transaction within specified period thereby not leaving any room for uncertainty?  The time
limit within which the parties should decide should also be specified.
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
This is a discretion provided to the secured creditor to accept payment for sale of immovable property even after the statutory
period of 15 days depending on the merit of the case.  Otherwise, the fixed period may, in some cases, fail the sale transition even if the
case merits extension of time for payment beyond prescribed time limit.  Hence, the flexibility.
 
14.       Point raised- Rule 9(7)
Where the immovable property sold is subject to any encumbrances, the authorized officer may, if he thinks fit, allow the
purchaser to deposit with him the money required to discharge the encumbrances and any interest due thereon together with such
additional amount that may be sufficient to meet the contingencies or further cost, expenses and interest as may be determined by him.
(a)    If the property sold is subject to any encumbrance, why the purchaser has been made liable to pay for discharging such
encumbrances?
(b)   The rule confers wide discretion upon the authorized officer in determining additional amount that may be sufficient to meet the

169th Report of Committee on Subordinate Legislation
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/169threport.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:52]
contingencies of further cost, expenses and interest without any approval or control of either the Board of Directors of the secured
creditor; should there not be some checks to avoid its misuse?
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
(a ) The person, who purchases the property, takes it subject to the subsequent encumbrances, if any, it possess, with the full
knowledge thereof.  Hence, if he desires to have the property free of encumbrance, he shall take steps to get the encumbrance discharged. 
This is, therefore, an enabling provision.  Also, it may be noted that in terms of sub-Rules (8) to (10), the authorized officer, who received
the payment to the party entitled to the payment pursuant to release of encumbrance, deliver property free of encumbrance (known to the
secured creditor) to the purchaser and issue sale certificate indicating the sale free of any encumbrance known to the secured.  Thus, it is
the choice of the purchase to purchase the property subject to encumbrance or free of encumbrance.
(b ) The suggestion of the Committee can be considered i.e. to provide for approval of the secured creditor as to the
additional amount required from the purchaser to discharge the subsequent encumbrance.
 
Action Taken by the Ministry : (29.11.2006)
The authorized officer is a responsible officer who will discharge his functions strictly in accordance with law.  When a property
is sold subject to any encumbrances, there may be some expenditure to discharge the encumbrances and to meet contingencies of further
costs.  The authorized officer must have the discretion to determine the amount.   To make such determination subject to the approval of
the Board of Directors or the Board of Trustees would only mean further delay and adding another layer of decision making to what is a
normal administrative matter.  Government is of the view that there is no need to add a layer of approval by the Board of Directors or the
Board of Trustees in order to check possible misuse.  If, in any case, misuse is brought to the notice of the Board of Directors or the
Board of Trustees, they could always revise the order of the authorized officer or take suitable action against him.  We should not add
more and more layers to decision making in what are purely administrative matters.   The only safeguard that we may add to Rule 9(7) is
making a proviso that if any money remains unspent out of the deposit made by the purchaser, after meeting the cost of removing
encumbrances and contingencies, that amount shall be returned to the purchaser.  It is therefore, suggested that following proviso may be
added below sub-rule (7) of Rule 9.
“Provided that if after meeting the cost of removing encumbrances and contingencies there is any surplus available out of the
money deposited by the purchaser such surplus shall be paid to the purchaser within 15 days from the date of finalisation of the sale”
 
15.       Point raised- Rule 9(8)
On such deposit of money for discharge of the encumbrances, the authorized officer may issue or cause the purchaser to issue
notices to the persons interested in or entitled to the money deposited with him and take steps to make the payment accordingly.
Should the word “may” in the above stated rule not be replaced by the word “shall” to make it obligatory for the authorised officer
or purchaser to issue notices to the interested or entitled persons?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
The suggestion of the committee seems to be reasonable and can be considered.
 
Action Taken by the Ministry : (29.11.2006)
In the Rule 9(8), the word ‘may’ may be substituted by the word ‘shall’.
 
16.       Point raised- Rule 10(1)
The Board of Directors or the Board of  Trustees, as the case may be, may appoint in consultation with the borrower
any person (hereinafter referred to as the Manager) to manage the secured assets the possession of which has been taken
over by the secured creditor.
(a)
    Should the word “may” not be replaced by the word “shall” in the rule to make it obligatory for the secured creditor to associate
the borrower also in the appointment of the manager?
(b)   Should some qualifications not be prescribed for the person to be appointed as Manager?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
(a)       The suggestion of the Committee may be accepted for a limited extent of consultation.  Association, in the sense of his approval,
will be an hindrance to the process of appointing the Manager.
(b)       The suggestion of the Committee can be considered.   The qualifications, as prescribed in sub-section (1) (b) (i) of section 10 of
the B.R.Act can be considered.
 
            Action Taken by the Ministry : (29.11.2006)
Sub-Section (1)(b) (i) of the Section 10 of the B.R.Act specifies that a banking company shall not employ or continue the
employment of any person who is, or at any time, has been adjudicated insolvent, or has suspended payment or has compounded with his
creditors, or who is, or has been convicted by a Criminal Court of an offence involving moral turpitude.   Other than the above no
qualification has been prescribed to be appointed as “Manager”.
The Rule may read as follows:
Rule 10(1)
“The Board of Directors or the Board of Trustees, as the case may be, may appoint in consultation with the borrower any person

(hereinafter referred to as the Manager) to manage the secured assets the possession of which has been taken over by the secured creditor.
“Provided that the Manager so appointed shall not be a person who is, or at any time has been, adjudicated insolvent, or has

17.       Point raised- Rule 10(2)
The Manager appointed by the Board of Directors or Board of Trustees, as the case may be, shall be deemed to be an
agent of the borrower and the borrower shall be solely responsible for the commission or omission of acts of the Manager
unless such commission or omission are due to improper intervention of the secured creditor or the authorized officer.
The Manager is appointed only in consultation with the borrower and seemingly he is not exercising any control over him.  In
such a case fixing the sole responsibility for the acts of commission or omission of Manager on the borrower seems to be unreasonable;
what are the documents of Ministry in this behalf?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
Although the Manager is appointed by the secured creditor to manage these secured assets, the possession of which is already
taken by the secured creditor, the secured creditor continues to be the mortgage only and the ownership remains with the borrower.  
However, since the control over the property passes with the possession to the secured creditor for realization of dues, very little control
remains with the borrower to deal with the property.  Hence, there is a merit in the suggestion of the Committee, particularly when only
consultation and not approval of the borrower is required for appointment of a manager.  Hence, the provision need reconsideration.
           
Action Taken by the Ministry : (29.11.2006)
The Rules as it stands, carves out an exception where any acts of omission or commission are due to the improper intervention of
the secured creditor or the authorized officer and in such a case the borrower is not responsible.  The provisions contained in sub rule (2)
of rule 10 are on the lines of the provisions contained in sub section (3) of section 69A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882.  The said
section was inserted by an amendment Act 20 of 1929 and the Government is of the view that there is no need to change the existing
provision.
 
18.       Point raised- Rule 11(1)
An application for recovery of balance amount by any secured creditor pursuant to sub-section (10) of Section 13 of
the Ordinance shall be presented to the Debts Recovery Tribunal in the form annexed as Appendix VI to these rules by the
authorized officer or his agent or by a duly authorized legal practitioner, to the Registrar of the Bench within whose
jurisdiction his case falls or shall be sent by registered post addressed to the Registrar of Debts Recovery Tribunal.
It has not been stated specifically in the rule as to who will appoint the duly authorized legal practitioner?
 
            Ministry’s comments : (7.5. 2004)
An application for recovery of balance amount by any secured creditor shall be presented by authorized legal practitioner or
authorized officer or his agent.  Hence, only the secured creditor can appoint the legal practitioner.

Delhi Advocates' Welfare Fund Rules, 2001.
 
            The Delhi Advocates' Welfare Fund Rules, 2001 framed under the Advocates' Welfare Fund Act, 2001 were examined
and a questionnaire on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Law & Justice (Department of Legal Affairs) on the 17 th
January, 2003 for furnishing their comments. The Ministry vide  their communication dated the 12 th May, 2005 furnished their
comments.
 
            The Committee considered the subject matter at its meeting held on 24th October, 2005. The points raised and Ministry's
comments are as follows: -
 
1)         Point referred (Rule 9(8) )-
 
"The Chairperson or the person presiding over a meeting shall have and exercise a second or a casting vote in all cases of
equality of votes."
Would it not be more appropriate if the Chairman does not exercise voting right in the normal course but votes only to
remove the tie?
            Ministry's Comments (12.05.05):-
The suggestion that the Chairman, who exercises the voting right only to remove the tie, is appreciated. The casting vote
in all cases of equality appears to be vague.
2)         Point referred (Rule 9(12) )-
 
"Meeting of the Trustee Committee shall, ordinarily, be held at its Office."
 
            The word 'ordinarily' used in the Regulation appears to be vague. Under what circumstances, meeting of the Committee
may be held at the places other than its office?        
Ministry's Comments (12.05.05):-
            The Rule as it exists appears to be in order. Of course, it impliedly gives the power to hold the meeting at any other place
other than its office if it is not ordinarily possible to hold the meeting at its office.
 
3)         Point referred (Rule 12(1) )-
 
"The Bar Council of Delhi may issue a certificate of recognition in Form IV, after such enquiry as it deems necessary, on
the application, made under Rule II."
            Rule 12(2
)- "The Bar Council of Delhi may recognize more than one association of advocates functioning at a particular
court, tribunal or other authority."
            Rule 12(3
)- "The Bar Council of Delhi shall prepare list of recognized association of advocates and update the same
from time to time."
 
(a)        Whether the Ministry have any objection in prescribing a specific time period within which certificate for recognition
may be issued to the association of advocates.
(b)        There is no provision in the rule for appeal/review if the application for recognition is rejected. The Ministry may please
comment.
            Ministry's Comments (12.05.05):-
(a) A period of four months initially may be prescribed for issuing a certificate for recognition.
(b) It would be appropriate if appeal can be prescribed, for which adjudicating authority may be the State Bar Council of
each State.
 
 
4)         Point referred (Rule 13(2))-
 
 "An advocate having membership in more than one association of advocates shall so apply from any one of them."
Why Rule 13(2) contemplates membership of more than one association of advocates, when an advocate can apply only
through one association? Should the rules not prohibit membership of more than one association by an advocate?
            Ministry's Comments (12.05.05):-
            The Rule appears to be clear that an advocate can apply from any one of the associations. The Rule appears to be
reasonable and requires no change.
 
 
5)         Point referred (Rule 14)
-

            The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (Conditions of Service of Officers and other Employees)
Regulation, 2000 framed under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority Act, 1999 were examined and a copy of
the questionnaire was forwarded to the Ministry of finance (Insurance Division) of the 27
th July, 2001, for which
comments/clarification were furnished thereon, by the Ministry, which were placed before the Committee.
 
2.         The points referred to the Ministry and their comments/clarifications thereon are reproduced below: - 
Q.No. 1:-
 (27/07/2001)   
            The Regulations are meant to regulate the conditions of service of officers and employees of Insurance Regulatory and
Development Authority. The word 'employees' has been defined in Regulation 3(1) (e) what is meant by "other employees" as
appearing in the short title as well as at other places in the Regulations?
Ministry’s Comments :- (14/03/2002)
            IRDA has reported that the word "other employees" means Class II, III and IV employees i.e. other than officers as
specified in the regulations, The language has been taken from Section 12(2) of the IRDA Act, 1999.
 
Q, No.2:-
 Regulation 4(2) classification of Officers and other employees: (27/07/2001)   
            " The number of posts, their classification, scale of pay, age limit, education and other qualifications, period of
probation, method of recruitment, composition of selection committee or departmental promotion committee shall be such as
may be determined by the authority."
            Why these details have not been mentioned in the regulations itself. Whether Ministry has any objection in defining
them in the regulations it or whether any other set of regulations will be framed for the purpose?
Ministry’s Comments:- (14/03/2002)
            IRDA has reported that details of number of posts, their classification, scale of pay, age limit, education and other
qualification, period of probation, method of recruitment, composition of selection committee of departmental selection
committee have not been mentioned in the regulations as these will form part of administrative orders to be issued from time to
time. The Insurance Advisory Committee which was consulted at the time of framing of these regulations felt that necessary
flexibility should remain with the Authority to attract, retain and reward talent. In addition, keeping in mind the dynamic nature
of work involved, the staffing requirements of the Authority would vary and any watertight classification may hinder its
effective and efficient functioning.

:-  Regulation 10 Promotion against sanctioned post: (27/07/2001)

Authority and shall be based on-
(a)        Merit, suitability and seniority in cases of Class I and II posts:
(b)        Seniority and merit in cases of Class III and Class IV posts:
Provided that in assessing the suitability of officers and other employees to promotion posts, the Competent Authority

Ministry’s Comments:- (14/03/2002)
            IRDA has reported that word "suitability" has been included deliberately in the regulations as a situation may so arise
that a person in spite of being meritorious and senior in a particular cadre may not be possessing the necessary skills and
temperament to handle certain specialized assignments. Technical skills are also to be predominantly available with a person to
function effectively. Posts in the regulatory authority shall require technical as well as administrative skills, Combination of

th June, 2003 for their comments/clarifications thereon.

and the Committee’s observations thereon during its visit to Mumbai are reproduced below:-

            The Regulations have been laid on the table of both the Houses of Parliament.   They were laid in the Rajya Sabha on
14.12.1994 and in the Lok Sabha on 19.12.1994.

have been framed much earlier.

            “These regulations may be called “The Transport, Handling and Storage of Dangerous Goods in Bombay Port
Regulations, 1994” and are framed under the provisions of clauses (f) and (n) of section 123 of Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 (38
of 1963) made by the Port of Bombay”.
The date of commencement of these regulations has not been indicated which is an essential component of any
rule/regulation.  The Ministry may please indicate the date of commencement of these regulations in the regulations itself.
Ministry’s reply

Point-3: Regulation 4.4 (iii) – Dangerous Goods
            “Dangerous Goods mean goods which by reason of the nature, quantity or mode of storage of such goods are either
singly or collectively liable to endanger the life or the health of the persons within the port limits or on a vessel or to cause
damage to property within such port limits and includes such goods contained in a receptacle, portable tank, freight container or
vehicle as defined in the IMDG Code.  The term includes an empty receptacle, portable tank or tank vehicle which as been
previously used for carriage of dangerous goods unless such receptacle has been cleaned and dried or when the nature of the
former contents permits such carriage with safety and allow the containers to be closed securely.
Dangerous goods include all substance
(i)
                  Having properties coming within the classes listed in the IMDG Code;
(ii)                Substance defined as explosive as defined by the Explosive e Act, 1884 and /or the Explosive Rules, 1983;
(iii)               Any other goods which the competent authority may specify as dangerous goods;
(iv)              Hazardous chemicals listed in Schedule-1 of the Manufacture, Storage and Import of Hazardous Chemicals Rules,
1989”.
The regulation gives discretionary powers to the competent authority to specify and good as dangerous one.  Whether
such powers are exercised judiciously and are not liable to be misused?
Ministry’s reply
            Classification of the dangerous goods is based on International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code (IMDG Code). 
However, new types of hazardous chemicals are being manufactured, transported and traded.   Thus, Port may be called upon to
handle new chemicals before they are classified and listed under IMDG Code.  Hence, the Port has been vested with
discretionary powers to handle such chemicals.  However, these powers are exercised judiciously as the decision is based on the
chemical composition details of such goods obtained from the manufacturers and the importers/exporters.   Under the
circumstances Competent Authority has been assigned some discretionary powers.
Committee’s observation
The Committee noted the explanation given by the Ministry.

            “Inspector of Dangerous goods for the purpose of the regulations means a person appointed by the Competent Authority
to ensure compliance with these rules at any handling, storage, disposal or transport of the dangerous goods coming to this port”

Inspector of Dangerous Goods?
Ministry’s reply
            The Asstt. Manager (Hazardous Cargo) has been appointed as the Inspector of Dangerous Goods under these regulations
and he is responsible for carrying out the responsibilities under these regulations.  For appointment to this post, the requirements
are laid down and include minimum post graduate qualification in Chemistry and experience of 5 years in handling, stowage and
storage of dangerous and hazardous chemicals in a factory or a manufacturing industry.  Besides, the incumbent is also given
training from time to time to keep pace with the new developments with regard to dangerous cargo, their safe storage and
transportation, etc.
Committee’s observation

Inspector of dangerous goods should be indicated in the regulations itself.

            On board the vessel, the Master of the vessel is generally the responsible person.  The Master has the necessary
knowledge and experience to carry dangerous goods in compliance with IMDG Code as he is certified by the Maritime
Licensing Authority of the country from where he has obtained his Certificate of Competency as Master.  The Master is thus

service regulations and all other rules relating to the service matters as that of IDBI. IDBI Pension Regulations were notified in
1995 and have been made applicable w.e.f. November 01, 1993. In terms of the sixth bi-partie settlement between the IBA and

fixing the interest on arrears at the time of re-admission at not exceeding 3%.
            (ii) To prescribe a period of 15 days to ensure continuity of the membership of the fund and that the membership may be
discontinued if the member failed to respond.
            Point 6 (Rule 15
):  To prescribe 6 months period for the issuance of certificate of membership to the fund.

the State roll to the Trustee Committee.
            Point 8 (Rule 19): 
To substitute the word 'thiery' with the word 'thirty', thereby rectifying a typographical error.
 
On rest of the points the Committee notes with satisfaction the explanation furnished by the Ministry.
 
            The Committee, however recommends that the Ministry of Law and Justice should carry out modification in the Rules as
agreed to by them, expeditiously.
 
III
            The Committee notes with satisfaction that IRDA have taken a decision to implement the Government orders on
reservations for the reserved category persons and allow to them suitable relaxation in age, educational qualification,
experience, etc. The Committee recommends that the policy decision of IRDA should find a clear mention in their Regulation,
so that the policy gets a statutory recognition. As regard to the autonomy conferred upon IRDA in the matter of recruitment and
promotion, the Committee feel that the justification given for the autonomy may no doubt sound appealing, but vesting of wide 
discretion  in any authority is always liable to be misused.
 
While the Committee appreciates the need for autonomy as projected by the IRDA, but in the Committee’s view,
subordinate legislation in the form of Rules/ Regulations should be codified to the optimum, particularly when they to regulate
the recruitment/promotion policy of an organization which has a bearing on its manpower. Accordingly, the Committee
recommends that IRDA may review their regulations to see to what extent they can do away with the element of subjectivity, of
course without compromising with their efficiency standards.
IV
           
The Committee notes with satisfaction that the Ministry of Shipping, Road Transport and Highways, (Department of Shipping)
have taken necessary action on almost all of its recommendations as follows:

The Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998.

and a questionnaire on the subject was forwarded to the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution,
(Directorate of Vanaspati, Vegetable Oils & Fats) on the 29
th September, 1999 for their comments/clarifications thereon.   The

1.       Point raised
Whether the Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998 has been laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha, if so, the
details in this regard.
Ministry’s Comments
41 copies of the Edible Oils Packaging (Regulation) Order, 1998 issued vide Notification NO. GSR. 584 (E) dated 17-
09-1998 and Corrigendum No. GSR 702 (E) dated 30-11-1998 alongwith one copy of each in Hindi and in English
authenticated by the Minister (Consumer Affairs and Public Distribution) were sent to both Lok Sabha and Rajya  Sabha
Secretariats on 10-12-1998 vide this Directorate’s letter No. 17/1/98-EXP. dated 09-12-1998. While information from Lok
Sabha regarding laying of the papers on the Table on 15-12-1998 (vide Lok Sabha Bulletin Part –I No. 58) has been received,
the information from Rajya Sabha has not be received so far.
 
2.       Point raised- 
Clause 2(b)
          “Edible Oils” mean  vegetable oils and fats and include any i.e, margarine, vanaspati, bakery shorting and fat spread as
specified in the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (37 of 1954) and rules made there under, for human consumption;”
Whether the term “edible oils” include ghee and butter also and if not, the justification for non-inclusion of these items
within the meaning of the term.
Ministry’s Comments
The term “Edible Oils” does not include ghee and butter, as ghee and butter are of animal origin and not of vegetable
origin. The term “edible oils” means vegetable oil as per the definition of “edible oils”
 
3.       Point raised- Clause 2(c)
          “Edible Oils Commissioner” means the person appointed as Edible Oils Commissioner by the Central Government and
includes any other person empowered by the Central Government to exercise any or all of the functions of the Edible Oils
commissioner under this Order;”
Whether there are any qualifications or conditions precedent to empowering any person to exercise any or all the
functions of the Edible Oil Commissioner and if so, whether Government have any objection in prescribing them in the Order
itself.
Ministry’s Comments
No qualification has been explicitly stated. The implicit understanding is that the person empowered to exercise the
functions of the Edible Oils Commissioner would be a Senior Gazetted Officer of the Central/ State Government competent
enough to handle the responsibility of the job assigned and enjoying the confidence of the superiors.
 
Action Taken
Modified the provision of Clause 2 (c) of the Order vide notification dated 22 nd November, 2005 (Annexure VII-
Appendix ‘A’)
 
4.       Point raised- 
Clause 3(b)
          “which is not packed in a container, marked and labeled in the manner as specified in the Scheule-1:
                  Provided that the State Government may, in the public interest, for reasons to be recorded in writing, in specific
circumstances and for a specific period by a notification in the Official Gazette, exempt any edible oil from the provisions of
this Order.”
What is the justification for empowering the State Governments to exempt any edible oil from the provisions of this
Order? What are the specific circumstances in the mind of the Ministry behind prescribing for such exemption? Further, there

PARLIAMENT OF INDIA
file:///10.21.218.119/who%20am%20i/1%20rajesh%20sir/convert/english/Committee%20on%20Subordinate%20Legislation/172%20Report.htm[25-10-2016 16:42:19]
is no provision in the clause under which the State Government is under any obligation to inform the Central Government or
the Edible Oils Commissioner regarding the exemption given to any edible oil. Whether such information is not desirable in the
opinion of Government; what is the reaction of the Ministry in this regard? Whether these provisions are being implemented in
a foolproof manner?
Ministry’s Comments
The Central Government is aware of the fact that the production of edible oils is highly decentralized. Substantial
quantity is produced in the small scale or unorganized sector. Further, a sizeable portion of the population is living below the
poverty line. It is in view of these situations that the State Governments have been empowered to exempt any edible oil from
the provisions of this Order in specific circumstances and for specific period only in the public interest for reasons to be
recorded in writing and for specific period only.
          Further vide 
Clause 15, the Edible Oil Commissioner has been authorized to issue appropriate directions including
seeking of information from the State Governments for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of the Packaging Order.
 
5.       Point raised- Clause 4(1) read with Schedule-III
“Registration: No person shall carry on business as a packer except under a certificate of registration granted to him
under this Order and in accordance with the terms and conditions specified in the Schedule-III.”
One of the terms and conditions for grant of certificate of registration is that the registered packer shall not employ any
person who is suffering from infection/contagious disease which is likely to affect packing in hygienic conditions. Which is the
authority that would determine whether any particular disease is infectious or contagious; whether Government have any
objection in prescribing the competent authority in the Order itself? Further, it has been made obligatory for each registered
packer to maintain a register showing the quantity sold. Is it not possible that a registered packer may not be engaging himself
in selling, the product and that he might be doing only the packaging work, in that case such a registered packer would not be
able to comply with this condition and he would be unable to keep a record of the edible oil sold. Whether Government have
any objection in suitable modification of this condition? 
Ministry’s Comments
The power for implementation of the Packaging Order is delegated to the State Governments. It has been left to the State
Governments to decide as to how they will carry-out the various provisions of the order. We have already written to the State
Governments that in case there is any operational difficulty in the implementation of the Order, these may be brought to the
notice of the Central Government so as to resolve the issue in a manner which is not inconsistent with the provisions of this
Order.
 
6.       Point raised- 
Clause 4(2)
          “Every person who intends to carry on the business of a packer shall make an application to registering authority in the
Form specified in the Schedule-II together with the fee to be paid to the State Government, in such manner as may be specified
by the State Government.”
The provision does not specify the quantum of fee to be paid to the State Government along with the application form to
the registering authority. What is the justification for not prescribing the quantum of fees and the manner in which it could be
paid?
Ministry’s Comments
          As already indicated, the power for implementation of the Packaging Order has been delegated to the State Government.
It has been left to the State Government to specify the quantum of fee having regard to the local situations etc.

Act 17 of 1982 with effect from 31.5.1982.
Committee’s observation
          The Committee was appraised that the regulations were not laid on the table of both the Houses as there was no
laying provision in the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 prior to 1982.  The Committee desired that the regulations should
be laid now alongwith the amendments suggested by it.

Ministry’s reply
          Section 124 (1) of the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 provides that no regulation made by the Board under the Act

regulation is accordingly worded for the regulations to come into effect from date of publication of Government’s

“A pilot shall at all times exercise strict sobriety.  He shall, throughout the time he is in charge of vessel, use his
utmost care and diligence for her safety and the safety of other vessels and property.  He shall when necessary keep
the lead going while the vessel is underway.  He shall not lay by the vessel aground without a written order from the
owner or officer in command.”
(a)      Whether the Board has prescribed any code of conduct for the pilots, and if so, whether the same cannot
be made part of the regulations?
(b)     What action is taken for violation of code of conduct?
Ministry’s reply
(a)      The Board has not prescribed any code of conduct specifically for the Pilots apart from the above
provisions of regulations 27 and 28.  However, Mumbai Port Trust Employees (Conduct) Regulations, 1976, which
contain various regulations regarding discipline, integrity, devotion to duty, etc., are applicable to all employees of the
Port including the Pilots.  Since the Pilots perform certain specific tasks relating to navigation, docking, undocking,
towing, mooring, etc. of the ships, in addition, certain specific provisions have been made in these regulations, namely,
in regulations 27 and 28.
(b)     Violation of code of conduct under regulations 27 and 28 and the general code of conduct prescribed
under the Mumbai Port Trust Employees (Conduct) Regulations, 1976 invites action/penalty under the Mumbai Port
Trust Employees (Classification, Control & Appeal) Regulations, 1976.
(11)    Point referred: Regulation 33 - Pilot may leave vessel at anchor in the 
harbour if not provided with
proper food and sleeping accommodation
          “The Master of a vessel in pilotage  charge of a Pilot shall provide the Pilot with reasonable accommodation, if
necessary, and with breakfast between 7.00 a.m., with lunch between 8.00 p.m., if the vessel is at anchor in the
harbour during these hours.  In the event of failure on the part of the Master of the vessel, the pilot may leave the
vessel and come to shore after giving the officer in command at least one hour’s notice in writing of his intention to do
so and shall report the case in writing to the Deputy Conservator as soon as practicable.”
(a)      What is implied by the term – “reasonable accommodation”?
(b)     To what extent the provisions of regulation 33 are still being implemented, are these provisions which
require reporting in writing twice not obsolete in the present day scenario?
Ministry’s reply
(a)      Reasonable accommodation means an accommodation which would provide the pilot adequate comfort
and be suitable to his status under the attendant circumstances and conditions.  Usually, as a matter of international
practice, all sea-going vessels have specified accommodation for pilot known as Pilot’s cabin.
(b)     The provision is not so relevant in today’s scenario where berthing of vessel does not take such long time
as before nor does a vessel needs to stay for long period at anchorage awaiting docking.  However, if the rare occasion
of a pilot having to leave the vessel does arise, giving of notice to Master of the vessel is necessary.  Likewise, report
to the Dy. Conservator is essential to have full information and enable enquiry into the situation and taking of
corrective action as may be necessary.
Committee’s observation

Schedule-III
Against the eligibility column for various posts covered in the schedule, a minimum period of service has been

higher scale.  In the same breath, there is a proviso for relaxation in the qualifying service for a period up to 2 years,

6.       Point raised
Schedule-III
For appointment to the posts in the Schedule, the method of promotion has been stated to be on the basis of
seniority-cum-merit.
What are the main features of this procedure for promotion; Whether it is permissible to change the seniority of
officials as it exists in the feeder grade while recommending their names for promotion to the next higher grade which
is inherent in the “selection” as a method of promotion at least for the purpose of promotion in scale III, scale II and
scale I so as to promote merit in the organisation?
Ministry’s reply
“Seniority-cum-merit” shall mean seniority and found fit for promotion.   It is not possible to change the
seniority of officials, as it exists in the feeder grade.  Thus, seniority-cum-merit implies promotions based on seniority
subject to minimum necessary merit requisite for the promotion.  The Government feels that there should be a uniform
criterion for promotion to all scales and that the present system may continue.
Committee’s Observation
The Committee came across divergent views on the point of promotion on the basis of seniority-cum-merit.  The
Bank of Rajasthan was of the view that promotion should not be purely on the basis of seniority only and merit should
also be given at least 50% weight age.  The Dungarpur Banswara Gramin Bank was of the view that in lower scales,
weight age may be given to seniority but in higher scale merit should prevail.   The Gramin Bank was of the view that
promotion should be made on the basis of both seniority and merit.  The Committee reiterated the need for balance
between seniority and merit to keep the Regional Rural Banks competitive with the other commercial banks.
Action taken
The existing recruitment rules provide for filling up the posts by seniority-cum-merit.   It, therefore, gives due
weightage to the seniority as well as merit.    However, the position would be reviewed after the process for
amalgamation is completed.

pilots may leave vessels at anchor in the harbour if not provided with proper food and sleeping accommodation.
 
8.       The Committee is happy to note that the Ministry has revised the whole set of regulations of 1975, made them
more relevant to the current times and also complied with the requirement of laying the regulations before the
Parliament which could not be done in the case of 1975 regulations due to the absence of such a provision in the Major
Port Trusts Act, 1963.
 
 
 
III
 
The Regional Rural Banks (Appointment and Promotion of Officers and other Employees) Rules, 1998 –
Implementation of the recommendations of the Committee as contained in its 157
th Report.
 
The Committee noted with satisfaction that the Ministry of Finance, Department of Economic Affairs have taken
necessary action on its recommendations on Rules 4, 10(1), 10(1) proviso and Schedule III and notified the necessary
amendments. On the remaining points, the Committee notes with satisfaction the explanation furnished by the
Ministry.
 
IV
The Export of Live Fish (Quality Control, Inspection and Monitoring)
Rules, 2002 – Implementation of 157th Report of the Committee.
 
The Committee considered the response of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (Department of Commerce)
on the recommendations of the Committee on rules 9 and 14 and going by the explanation furnished decided not to
pursue its recommendations on these two rules any more.

Approved valuer means the professional who is qualified to value the property for a fee.  It is difficult to

6.       The Committee notes with satisfaction that IRDA have taken a decision to implement the
Government orders on reservations for the reserved category persons and allow to them suitable relaxation
in age, educational qualification, experience, etc. The Committee recommends that the policy decision of
IRDA should find a clear mention in their Regulation, so that the policy gets a statutory recognition. As
regard to the autonomy conferred upon IRDA in the matter of recruitment and promotion, the Committee
feel that the justification given for the autonomy may no doubt sound appealing, but vesting of wide 
discretion  in any authority is always liable to be misused.
 
While the Committee appreciates the need for autonomy as projected by the IRDA, but in the
Committee’s view, subordinate legislation in the form of Rules/ Regulations should be codified to the
optimum, particularly when they are to regulate the recruitment/promotion policy of an organization which
has a bearing on its manpower. Accordingly, the Committee recommends that IRDA may review their
regulations to see to what extent they can do away with the element of subjectivity, of course without
compromising with their efficiency standards.

      The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 2005  
 
 The Determination of the Price of the Forfeited Property Rules, 
2005 framed under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 were 
examined and certain points, which needed further 
comments/clarifications, were put together in the form of a questionnaire. 
It was forwarded to the Ministry of Home Affairs for their 
comments/clarifications on July 10, 2006.  In reply, the Ministry of Home 
Affairs vide their communication dated October 16, 2006 informed as 
follows :- 
“….that the comments of Rajya Sabha Secretariat 
were examined and draft   comments were sent to the 
Ministry of Law for vetting.  The Ministry of Law has 
accepted the comments of Ministry of Home Affairs in Rule 
6.  The Comments in Rule 3, 5(1), 5(2), 7(1) and 7(2) have 
been reexamined and fresh comments of this Ministry are 
enclosed. 
 
On receipt of the Rajya Sabha acceptance on the 
proposed comments/amendments, the approval of Hon’ble 
Home Minister will be obtained for notifying the same.” 
 
2. The   points   referred to the Ministry and their comments thereon 
are reproduced below : 
 
1.     Point raised:  Rule 3 : Appointment of Authorised Officer  
“Where the person against whom an order of forfeiture has been 
made (hereinafter referred to as the person), is acquitted, the property 
shall  be returned to him or his legal nominee and if it is not possible for 
any reason to return the forfeited property, the State Government shall 

appoint an officer not below the rank of Deputy Secretary to that 
Government, to be known as Authorised Officer, to evaluate and fix the 
price of the forfeited property with a view to compensating the person in 
lieu of the forfeited property.” 
As per Rule 3, all what has been said about the Authorised Officer 
is that he must not be below the rank of Deputy Secretary of the 
Government. As the job of evaluation is technical, should the Authorised 
Officer not possess some technical qualification also? 
 
 
Ministry's reply: 
In order to have a more cogent procedure for the authorized officer 
to compute the value of forfeited property, it is proposed that Rule 3 
may be amended by inserting an explanation which will allow the 
Authorized Officer to utilize the service of consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to 
arrive at the value of forfeited property. 
 
2.    Point raised: Rule 5 : Consideration of the representation : 
          "(1) The Authorised Officer shall take into account, representation, 
if any, made by the person or his leg al nominee before the final 
determination of the price with respect to the forfeited property is made" 
 Whether the Ministry have any objection in specifying a time frame 
for disposal of representation, if any, given by the person or his legal 
nominee or f or that matter for completing the whole process of 
determining the price of the forfeited property under the rules? 
 
Ministry's reply 

 180 days from the first day of the next month of the receipt of the 
representation. 
 
3.    Point raised: Rule 5: Consideration of the representation: 
 
          "(2) The Authorised Officer shall thereafter fix the price of the 
forfeited property and intimate the same in writing to the person or his 
legal nominee". 
 Rule 5 mentions that the Authorised Officer shall intimate the person 
or his legal nominee as to the fixing of the price of the forfeited property. 
Rule 6 maintains that the State Government should issue an order to the 
effect that the property stands sold to the State Government at the price 
fixed under rule 5. 
        Whether the intimation to the person/legal nominee is accompanied 
by such an order, or such an arrangement is being viewed as an assurance 
to the concerned individual. 
Ministry's reply: 
 Within 60 days from the date the proces s of determining the price of 
forfeited property is completed. 
 The persons/legal nominee is informed about the price of the forfeited 
property as per Rule 5(2) of the said Act. Further reference by the State 
Government to the Central Government about the Head of Account etc. 
is an administrative function only.  The M/o Law and Justice have opined 
that this appears to be sustainable. 
 
4.    Point raised : Rule 7: Deposit of the amount by the Central 
Government: 
 

           " (1) The Central Government shall on receipt of the order under 
rule 6, deposit the price fixed for the forfeited property in such Treasury 
or under such Head of Account as may be specified therein under 
intimation to the person or his legal nominee." 
 As the matter being of utmost urgency  to the affected individual, 
whether the Ministry have any objection in specifying a time -frame 
within which the Central Government, after receipt of such an order as 
specified in rule 6, deposit the forfeited property in such Treasury under 
such Head of A ccount as specified in such an order under intimation to 
the person or his legal nominee.   
 
Ministry's reply: 
 Within 30 days from the date of order as specified in Rule 6. 
 
5.    Point raised: Rule 7: Deposit of the amount by the Central 
Government: 
 
           " (2) The amount of price along with interest there on, shall be paid 
to the person  
Or to his legal nominee."  
   
           Sub-rule (2) of Rule 7 mentioned about payment of the price of the 
forfeited property along with "interest thereon". Wheth er Ministry will 
specify at what rate interest will be paid to the claimant? 
 
 
 
Ministry's reply: 

 It is proposed that the interest may be paid at the prevailing interest 
rates on savings bank account of State Bank of India.

Affairs on the points forwarded to them.  The Committee notes with 
satisfaction that the Ministry of Home Affairs have agreed to take action 
as follows in pursuance to its suggestions : 
(i) In Rule 3, to insert  an explanation allowing  the Authorized 
Officer to utilize the service of consultant(s)/Valuer(s) to 
arrive at the value of forfeited property.  In the existing rules, 
the Authorised Officer is required to do this job  without any  
assistance; and   
(ii) In Rule  7 (2), to  make provision for paying  the interest at

Bank of India on the price of the forfeited property to the 
claimant.  The existing provisions do no mention about  the 
rate of interest. 
 The Committee hopes that the Ministry would carry out the above 
amendments expeditiously under intimation to it. However, on other 
points, the Committee notes with satisfaction the reply given by  the 
Ministry of Home Affairs.
